To summarize, the key findings of our research, stated in one sentence that includes all relevant information, are that
hepatocytes of different zonal origin can be separated by a flow cytometer.
hepatocytes of different liver zones can be separated by a combination of selective AO staining and cell sorting.
hepatocytes of the proximal (AO positive) and distal region (AO negative) of the liver acinar can be separated according to their zonation by fluorescence activated cell-sorting.
In summary, our research is concerned with
the development of a new technique, which allows the separation of hepatocytes from different zonal regions of the liver.
the development of a new technique to obtain a zonal fractionation of hepatocytes.
a new approach to separate cells according to their position in the liver acinus.
In summary, a comprehensive and detailed conclusive statement would be that
the technique of AO staining and cell sorting described here is an excellent tool for the separation of cells of different zonal origin.
this method allows the separation of zonally pure hepatocytes from a rat liver.
this procedure provides the opportunity to isolate and study cells of a defined zonal origin.
A comprehensive summary for our work would be that
the acinar zonal distribution of hepatocytes can be preserved after cell separation and that sorted hepatocytes can be used to study zonally different functions of hepatocytes.
the acinar zonation of the liver is maintained in isolated hepatocytes, and that the zonal heterogeneity of hepatocytes can be preserved after cell sorting.
hepatocyte acinar zone separation by flow cytometry is a simple and reliable technique to obtain pure zonal cell populations.
The main takeaway from our work is that
flow cytometry is a useful tool to separate hepatocytes of different zonal origin.
the technique of flow cytometric cell sorting of fluorescently labeled cells can be used to obtain zonally separated hepatocytes.
the technique described is useful for studying the functional heterogeneity of the liver acinar cell populations.
